Name: Gentle Emote
Description: Mirror gentle-emote pixel-art frames on a Ulanzi D200 key.
Detail:
Gentle Emote turns a Ulanzi D200 key into a small screen for the gentle-emote avatar: the pixel-art Gentleman that acts out what a coding agent is doing. The plugin listens on a local port and shows whatever frame gentle-emote sends, so the key animates together with the terminal.

Core features:
1. Receives the gentle-emote external-display protocol v1 (HTTP POST with an image/png body and X-Emote-* metadata headers) on 127.0.0.1, port 8000 by default.
2. Scales each 64x64 frame with an exact 3x nearest-neighbour factor onto the 196x196 key grid, centred on a black canvas, so pixel-art edges stay crisp instead of blurring.
3. Offers an optional Fill scaling mode that stretches the frame across the whole key.
4. Falls back to the next free port when the configured port is already in use, and shows the port actually in use on the key while it waits for the first frame.
5. Keeps the newest frame only: the animation never lags behind the sender, because intermediate frames are dropped by design.
6. Needs no account, no cloud service, and no network beyond the local loopback interface.

Compatibility: Ulanzi D200 with Ulanzi Studio 2.1.4 or later on Windows 10+ and macOS 12+. Point gentle-emote's externalDisplay.url at the URL shown on the key (for example http://127.0.0.1:8000/emote). Pressing the key only redraws the current frame.
